After the update, the app applied a more efficient power profile because all five settings still matched the previous defaults. Testing showed that this profile substantially reduces idle CPU and radio wakeups while keeping the proxy usable on most networks.

Changed settings:
• Keep device awake: off
• Prepare WebSocket connections: off
• WebSocket keepalive: 180 seconds
• Route checks: off
• Cloudflare domain updates: off

If at least one power setting differed from the previous defaults, the entire profile was preserved. You can change these options at any time in Settings → Power usage if your network needs a more persistent background connection.

This app is a local MTProto bridge: Telegram connects to it on this device, and it forwards connections through direct WebSocket (WS), Cloudflare (CF), or direct TCP. It is not a VPN and affects only Telegram configured to use this proxy.\n\nThe app processes transport framing to route traffic. It does not decrypt message or media contents; remote transport services still carry the connection.

1. Tap Connect on the main screen.
2. Tap Open in Telegram.
3. Confirm and select this proxy in Telegram.
4. Open a chat to check the connection.

Valid settings are saved automatically. Only when you exit Settings does a running proxy restart, and only if the effective runtime settings changed. Appearance and statistics visibility apply immediately. After changing the port or secret, add the current proxy link in Telegram again.

Automatic mode normally uses WS → CF → TCP and default connection parameters, then adapts to observed Telegram traffic. Optional route probes are off by default. A network change resets route selection; internal restarts may retain the learned order.

If a direct WS media session stalls, the app closes that session and temporarily prefers CF for subsequent media connections to that datacenter. Telegram may recover by reconnecting, but recovery is not guaranteed.

Turn automatic mode off to configure routes, direct WS targets, and connection tuning manually. Manual values remain saved while automatic mode is enabled.

In manual mode, enable Cloudflare as an alternate route and choose whether to try it before WS or after WS fails. The fallback switch sets whether CF or TCP follows a failed WS attempt.

A custom Cloudflare domain replaces the shared list, rather than adding to it. HTTP 429 indicates rate limiting; the app puts that domain on a temporary cooldown.

Test and select a domain checks connection establishment to Telegram datacenters. A successful test does not prove that sustained media transfers will work.

In manual mode, each DC:IP line assigns a direct WebSocket target to a Telegram datacenter. Telegram chooses the datacenter; this app chooses how to reach it.\n\nRemoving a line leaves that datacenter to the enabled fallback routes. Keep the default targets unless troubleshooting a specific routing problem.

Manual connection tuning controls the transfer buffer and prepared WS pool size. The pool is used only when Prepare WebSocket connections is enabled; otherwise no prepared sockets are kept, and the manual pool size stays saved.\n\nThe default buffer is 256 KB. Larger buffers or pools consume more resources and do not necessarily improve speed. Change one value at a time to investigate a specific problem.

By default, Keep device awake, prepared WS connections, route probes, and shared-domain refresh are off. The WS keepalive interval is 180 seconds. Automatic routing still reacts to actual traffic when probes are off.\n\nKeeping the device awake may help with screen-off interruptions, but uses power and cannot guarantee network access. Prepared connections retain idle sockets; shorter keepalives send more frequent traffic. Adjust these only as needed: results depend on Android and the network.

Select System, Light, or Dark in the theme options. The app uses a Telegram-style palette unless Adaptive colors is enabled on Android 12 or newer, where it uses the device Material You palette.\n\nAppearance changes are saved and applied immediately without restarting the proxy.

Open Settings → Support and diagnostics → Diagnostic log. Logging runs while the app process is alive and keeps up to approximately 4 MB of recent technical events. Cleanup removes events older than 7 days. The bounded queue can drop events under load; share a report soon after a problem.

Message and media contents are not logged. Recognized proxy links, secrets, IP addresses, and sensitive fields are redacted, including during export, but review reports before sharing. Reports include app and OS details and the device model.

Clearing the log removes stored history, not previously exported or shared copies. Logging continues while the process is running.

First check that Telegram has the current proxy selected; remove old entries and add the current link again. Confirm internet access and complete any Wi-Fi sign-in. If the local port is occupied, stop the app using it or choose another port.

For stalled media, let Telegram reconnect or retry the download. In manual mode, try Cloudflare first and exit Settings to apply it. Test CF domains if needed, but a successful test does not guarantee media playback.

For screen-off failures, check Android background and battery restrictions; keeping the device awake may help. If the problem persists, review and share a diagnostic report soon after the failure, with a description of what stopped working.

There is no separate startup switch. Starting the proxy saves your intention to keep it enabled; after device startup the app attempts to restore it. Stop in the app or notification, or switching off the Quick Settings tile, cancels restoration. A process crash, system shutdown, or internal restart does not count as Stop.

If startup fails, the main screen offers Retry start and Stop so you can cancel restoration even while the proxy is not running. When upgrading from a version with the startup switch, its saved value is used initially; subsequent Start and Stop actions determine the behavior.

Android force-stop and background restrictions can prevent restoration. Reopen the app after force-stop and retry starting if needed. The service notification provides Restart and Stop controls; traffic display is optional.

Proxy running means the local service is active, not that Telegram can reach its servers. Check the separate connection status and try sending or loading something in Telegram.\n\nDetailed route and statistics displays are optional. Connection counters count connections, not people or messages. Pool hits show successful uses out of attempts, not the number of ready sockets. Zero hits are normal when prepared connections are disabled. Error counters include past failures and do not alone indicate a current outage.

Keep the listen address at 127.0.0.1 for access only from this device. 0.0.0.0 listens on all IPv4 interfaces and may expose the proxy to reachable networks. Do not share the proxy secret or link.\n\nThe TLS WebSocket client does not verify server certificates. Direct TCP adds no TLS layer. Telegram message encryption is separate from these transports; this app is not a VPN and does not promise anonymity.

Check for GitHub releases in About. For in-app downloads, the app verifies SHA-256, package identity, version, and signing certificate before handing the APK to the Android installer. These checks are not malware scanning.\n\nAndroid requires permission to install unknown apps and your confirmation to install. If no suitable download assets are available, the app opens the release page instead.
A local MTProto bridge for Telegram with WebSocket, Cloudflare, and direct TCP routes.
No root or separate app account required. No ads or analytics. The proxy runs on this device and connects through remote transport services.
Automatic or manual routing through WS, CF, and TCP. Prepared WebSocket connections are optional and off by default.
Includes a foreground service, notification controls, Quick Settings tile, and live statistics.
Inspired by tg-ws-proxy by Flowseal. Developed independently of Flowseal; not an official Telegram product.
Not a VPN or an anonymity guarantee. The WS client does not verify server certificates; direct TCP adds no TLS. Telegram message encryption is separate.
Updates come from GitHub. In-app downloads are checked for SHA-256, package, version, and signing certificate; installation requires Android permission and your confirmation.
